title: Industry Standard EP
label: Aftershock
format: EP (vinyl; Aftershock was vinyl-only at the time)

type.basis: Coded for Creepy Crawler, the track with documented vocal versions.

sound.text: 'Creepy Crawler' has low horns 'like a Blaxploitation soundtrack' and G-funk synth squiggles.
His beats in general: 'crunchy eight-bit noises' around G-funk-style melodies, intricate syncopation, and a distorted 'gremlin' laugh tag.

context.text: Wikipedia describes it as Terror Danjah's breakthrough instrumental EP on Aftershock.
The blog says it stood out among the dozens of 12"s reaching London record shops at the time.

rels.other: Wiley – 'Take Chances' (XL Recordings, 2004, B-side to 'Pies'), a vocal version of 'Creepy Crawler'
Wiley and Breeze over 'Creepy Crawler' on the Sidewinder Bonus CD, mixed by Logan Sama

uncertainty: The full tracklist, catalogue number and month are unknown, and the format is not stated directly. The MusicBrainz mirror (mb.videolan.org) shows a 12" 'Industry Standard Trilogy EP' (Discogs 708293) with different tracks and no date; it was not used for this entry. The slowmotion.blog source is a personal blog.
tracklist: Fully instrumental; includes 'Creepy Crawler'. A separate later 'Industry Standard Trilogy EP' (Lifesaver / Radar / Stiff / Freak Show VIP) exists and should not be confused with it.

audit.note: Only 'Industry Standard Part 4 - EP' found (a later release); original 2004 EP not found.
Artist discography lists 'Industry Standard Part 4' (Electronic, 2009) and 'Gremlinz (The Instrumentals 2003-2009)' (Electronic), but not the 2004 EP.
Terror Danjah's Bandcamp lists other releases (Red Card Riddim, Invasion, Scene 1, Module); no Industry Standard EP.
